title: The Son
focus: the pain of a father's love

teacherSummary.text: Siddhartha's spoiled son, raised in wealth, despises the ferry life and his father's gentleness. Vasudeva advises letting the boy return to the world, but Siddhartha cannot let go. The son finally runs away, stealing the ferry money. Siddhartha follows to the city and stops at Kamala's old garden, realizing he must not pursue him. Vasudeva brings him home.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “You cannot love” slowly and put it in my own words: Looking at his son, who reminds him of Kamala, Siddhartha remembers her telling him long ago that he could not love. Next, craft. I notice the remark is blunt and short, and it returns from the past just when he is suffering for love. The strongest word is “love”: the word names exactly what he is now feeling for the first time, so her old judgment is being proved wrong and right at once. Then, effect. Why does Kamala's old remark come back to Siddhartha now? My answer: Kamala's old remark that he could not love comes back to Siddhartha now because he loves his son helplessly; the memory shows he has learned to love, and that love brings pain he cannot control.
